fixes.title: Normalize the augmentation column / Krylov seed before the augmented Pade-13 exponential
fixes.summary: dense_phi_action embeds the raw vector v as the augmentation column (crates/rodas5p-core/src/matrix_functions.rs:158) and matrix_exp_pade13 picks squarings from the 1-norm of that augmented matrix (crates/rodas5p-core/src/matrix_functions.rs:80-84), so ||v||=1e8 adds ~24 squarings and ~1e-8 relative error (E-06: 18/54 failures, all at ||v||=1e8). Fix at the oracle: scale the column by 1/||v||_inf (or 1/||v||_2), exponentiate, and multiply the extracted column by ||v||; phi_k is linear in v so this is exact in exact arithmetic and makes the squaring count depend only on ||scale*A||. Independently, projected_action (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:820-822) and projected_exponential_action_with_residual_estimate (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:989-1005) should seed the reduced input with e1 (not beta*e1) and multiply the reduced result (and the residual term) by beta, so the projected oracle never sees the physical scale even if a caller bypasses the core normalization.
fixes.verification: Re-run the E-06 harness (RUN/harness/src/bin/e06_phi_action.rs on exp/E-06/cases.json) against the patched crate: all 54 cases must satisfy relerr_k <= 2.2e-13 for k=0..4 (currently worst 1.58e-8 at ||v||=1e8) and the Rust-only proportionality probe phi(A,1e8 v) vs 1e8*phi(A,v) must agree to <1e-14 (currently ~1e-8). Add a rodas5p-core unit test `dense_phi_action_is_scale_invariant` looping s in {1e-8,1,1e8} over k=1..4 on an 8x8 nonnormal matrix and asserting relative deviation <= 1e3*eps; add an integrators test that krylov_phi_action on 1e8*f and f differ by <=1e-13 relative. Existing exponential_contracts / fused_exponential_contracts binaries must stay green with no tolerance edits.

fixes.title: Report a true KIOPS/Sidje residual at happy breakdown instead of error_estimate = 0
fixes.summary: All three Arnoldi loops declare happy breakdown when h_{m+1,m} <= 64*sqrt(eps)*max(1,|h_im|) (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:881,905-911; 1078,1094-1099; 1563-1564) and then certify converged=true with error_estimate 0 (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:1136-1150 zeroes the already computed residual; 940-951 returns 0 when the nested difference is not finite; the legacy path has no residual estimator at all). Fix: (a) never overwrite the residual: the Sidje/KIOPS first-term estimate |delta * h_{m+1,m} * beta * e_m^T phi_1(delta H_m) e_1| is already computed at 1005-1009 and is exactly the quantity that is small-but-nonzero at a near-breakdown (5.7e-7 in the F-011 case), so report it and decide convergence by `residual <= threshold`; (b) make breakdown a basis-extension stop, not a certificate: converged = residual <= threshold || h_next == 0.0 || full_space; if a happy breakdown leaves residual > threshold the substep loop at 1264-1325 already doubles substeps (delta halves, residual shrinks), which is the correct recovery; (c) legacy krylov_phi_action: replace the nested-difference-only estimator with the generalized first term |delta * h_{m+1,m} * beta * e_m^T phi_{k+1}(delta H_m) e_1| obtained from one extra dense_phi_action(h, scale, k+1, e1) row, so the first checkpoint and breakdown checkpoints carry a finite estimate; (d) tighten the breakdown constant to O(1e3*eps) relative to column_scale, since the residual now governs convergence and the loose 64*sqrt(eps) was only ever justified as a certificate.
fixes.verification: Port exp/D4/happy_breakdown.py into a Rust test: A=diag(-1,-3), v=e1+4.5e-7*e2, scale=1, rtol=1e-10: expect either converged=false (fused path then substeps) or error_estimate >= 3.9e-7 (true error) -- currently converged=true, estimate 0. Second case delta=1e-7, scale=3 (true rel err 1.0e-7). Assert adaptive_exponential phi_error_proxy is > 0 for that step. Run all prebuilt exponential test binaries from RUN/bin/MANIFEST.json; the prefix-parity tests (rtol 1e-12) must pass without tolerance changes; record any step-count changes in the exponential-lane receipts as a failure-preserving diff, not a tolerance edit.

fixes.title: Scale-aware fused combination: balance the augmented block and choose Pade squarings from ||A^k||^{1/k}
fixes.summary: fused_phi_linear_combination divides each term by scale^k (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:1357-1361), so for the pexprb54s4 endpoint terms (phi_3/phi_4 of O(h^2) remainders) the augmented operator (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:1174-1222) has a B block of norm O(c/h) that dominates the projected Hessenberg's 1-norm; matrix_exp_pade13 then over-squares (8 -> 17 squarings as h goes 0.1 -> 1e-4, rel err 7.5e-15 -> 9e-12, D4/pade_overscaling.out) because it uses only ||.||_1 (crates/rodas5p-core/src/matrix_functions.rs:80-84). Two complementary changes: (a) in matrix_exp_pade13 compute a2,a4,a6 from the unscaled matrix first, derive d4=||A^4||_1^{1/4}, d6=||A^6||_1^{1/6} and set squarings from alpha=max(d4,d6) instead of ||A||_1 (Al-Mohy-Higham 2009 style; for the nilpotent augmented chain alpha << ||A||_1), then rescale a2,a4,a6 by 4^-s,16^-s,64^-s -- zero extra matmuls; (b) apply the KIOPS/phipm diagonal balancing similarity D=diag(I_n, eta, ..., eta^p) with eta=2^-ceil(log2 max_k ||b_k||_2) to the augmented operator (B columns scaled by eta^{c+1}, chain entries by eta, start-vector tail by D^-1) so the B block has norm O(1) before Arnoldi; the physical components of the result are unchanged by the similarity. Together with FIX-1 the projected oracle then sees an operator whose norm is set by ||scale*A|| and not by 1/h^k.
fixes.verification: Port exp/D4/pade_overscaling.py's augmented matrices (nilpotent-chain augmented H with ||M||_1 = 4.06e5 at h=1e-4) into a rodas5p-core test and assert rel err vs a high-precision reference <= 1e-14 for h in {1e-1,1e-2,1e-3,1e-4} (currently 9e-12 at 1e-4); assert the chosen squaring count is <= the value for h=0.1. E-06 must stay all-pass after (a). For (b) add an integrators test that pexprb54s4_fused_step on a 2-D stiff problem at h in {1e-2,1e-3,1e-4} matches the exact-phi dense oracle to <= 1e-13 relative at every h (currently degrades with h). Check the prefix-parity tests at rtol 1e-12 remain green.

fixes.title: Physical-norm (WRMS-aware) Krylov threshold and a phi error proxy in the same units as the time error
fixes.summary: The fused Krylov threshold is atol + rtol*max(||current||_2, beta) (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:1134-1135, 1595-1596) where beta is the norm of the augmented start [b0;0;..;1] (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:1216-1218, 1053) so it is floored at rtol*1 regardless of ||f0||, and adaptive_exponential converts the summed L2 residual into h*sum/||scale||_2 (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/adaptive_exponential.rs:83-94) before max-ing with a WRMS time error (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/adaptive_exponential.rs:262-265). Fix: (a) compute the threshold from the physical part only: rtol*||current[..n]||_2 with beta replaced by ||b0||_2 (the augmented tail is a bookkeeping unit, not a physical magnitude); (b) let the caller pass the integrator's error_scale vector into FusedPhiKrylovConfig (optional `weights`); the residual vector is r_m = coeff * v_{m+1} with v_{m+1} = work/next_norm already in hand, so residual_wrms = |coeff| * wrms(v_{m+1}[..n], weights) costs no JVPs; converge when residual_wrms <= krylov_fraction (e.g. 0.1) and report it; (c) phi_error_proxy becomes h*sum(residual_wrms over substeps), directly comparable with the WRMS time error. Governance note: this changes accept/reject decisions, so receipts must be regenerated and any step-count change recorded as a failure-preserving diff, never a tolerance widening.
fixes.verification: Add a scale-invariance test: take one stiff 2-D problem and its rescaled copy y -> c*y (f -> c*f, atol -> c*atol) for c in {1e-3, 1e3}; the adaptive pexprb54s4 driver must produce identical accepted step sequences and Krylov dimensions (to rounding) -- currently the threshold floor rtol*1 makes the c=1e-3 run over-converge and the c=1e3 run under-converge. Add a unit test that phi_error_proxy equals wrms(residual_vector, scale)*h for a hand-built substep report. Compare exponential-lane scientific-validity receipts before/after and file the diff in the ledger.

fixes.title: Retain the work of failed exponential trials (accounted API everywhere)
fixes.summary: The level-1 prefix creates a local WorkCounters (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:2402) and every failure path drops it: require_fused converts converged=false into Err(LinearSolve) (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:2131-2140) and `?` propagates NonFinite, while the adaptive loop's Err arm (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/adaptive_exponential.rs:225-253) only bumps rejected_steps and pushes trial_work: None; work is accumulated only on Ok (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/adaptive_exponential.rs:258). Fix: adopt the existing `_accounted` pattern (crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/exponential.rs:3032-3060) for the whole step: kernels return Result<Report, AccountedFailure { error: CoreError, work: WorkCounters }> (or take `&mut WorkCounters` from the caller, as fused_phi_action already does), the substep-cap exhaustion at 1309-1322 keeps its counters attached, and the adaptive Err arm does counters.accumulate(failure.work), sets trial_work: Some(failure.work) and adds the work to diagnostics. Publish only the accounted entry points from the fair-AB harness so the exponential lane cannot undercount.
fixes.verification: Test: stiff problem with FusedPhiKrylovConfig{maximum_dimension: 2, maximum_substeps: 1} so require_fused fails; assert the adaptive driver's counters.jvp_calls and rhs_evaluations after one rejected trial equal the kernel-local counters captured in the failure (currently 0 for that trial) and that AdaptiveEarlyFlowDefectAttempt.trial_work is Some. Property: total work reported must be monotone non-decreasing in the number of trials. Re-run the rodas5p-fair-ab exponential-lane comparison from RUN/bin/MANIFEST.json before/after; the exponential lane's work totals may only increase; record the delta in the ledger.

fixes.title: Stiff, nonscalar, non-commuting order test for pexprb54s4 (and exprb43)
fixes.summary: declared_orders_are_observed_on_nonlinear_problem (crates/rodas5p-integrators/tests/exponential_contracts.rs:131-135) only uses square_problem (dimension 1, crates/rodas5p-integrators/tests/exponential_contracts.rs:9-28), where the Krylov space is exact and all phi functions commute, so the >=4.7 assertion cannot see Krylov truncation or stiff order reduction; the audit's exact-phi replica measured local order ~5.8 nonstiff but global order ~4.1 on a stiff 2-D problem with lambda=-1e4 (exp/D4/pexprb54s4_order.out). Add two tests: (a) a 2-D stiff nonlinear problem (y1' = lambda*(y1 - g(t)) + g'(t) + y2^2, y2' = -y2 + y1*y2, lambda=-1e4, non-commuting J and N) integrated with the fused kernel at tight Krylov tolerance over h where |lambda|h spans 1..100, asserting the observed global order in that regime and recording it as the documented stiff order (expected ~4.0-4.2; assert >= 3.8 as a failure-preserving floor, not 4.7) plus nonstiff local order >= 4.7 on the same problem with lambda=-1; (b) a 64-D diffusion-reaction problem run with maximum_dimension=4 (forcing Krylov truncation) whose reported phi error must be > 0 and whose order must still be measured, so truncation cannot silently pass. Update the ledger/receipt label from 'order 5' to 'order 5 (nonstiff), observed stiff order ~4' with the test as evidence.
fixes.verification: Run exp/D4/pexprb54s4_order.py to fix the expected slopes (nonstiff local 5.7-5.9 main / 4.8-5.0 embedded; stiff lambda=-1e4 global 4.08-4.15), then run the new test binary; it must reproduce those slopes within 0.2 with exact-phi config. The test fails if a future tableau or phi-path change drops the stiff order below 3.8 or the nonstiff order below 4.7; thresholds are frozen in the test with a comment citing the D4 run and may not be lowered (governance: no post-hoc widening).
